bull.b: Interim safety data showed no severe adverse events attributed to ENV-105 and side effects were manageable with standard supportive care, supporting continued clinical development.

ENV-105 is positioned as a complement to osimertinib intended to reverse acquired resistance, offering a potential approach to extend the effectiveness of existing therapy where alternatives are limited.
Collaboration with Bayer opens additional development opportunities in prostate cancer and broadens strategic options for the program beyond the initial lung cancer focus.

bear.b: The safety-only update contained no lung cancer efficacy signal, leaving clinical benefit unproven and making future efficacy readouts the primary driver of upside.
The small, safety-only nature of the update limits the ability to draw efficacy conclusions and increases uncertainty around the trial's potential to deliver meaningful patient benefit.
Absence of severe events in a limited cohort does not validate the resistance-resensitization hypothesis, so mechanistic benefit remains unconfirmed and dependent on larger controlled data.
